claims.text: Rapid thermal quenching immediately after precursor reduction kinetically traps noble-metal atoms in a homogeneous HEA nanoparticle state.
Inhibiting atomic mobility prevents phase separation.
Inhibiting atomic mobility prevents elemental segregation.
Inhibiting atomic mobility prevents uncontrolled nanoparticle morphology.
Cooling rate can be varied after high-temperature reduction while heating rate, maximum temperature, and precursor composition are held constant.
Rapid quenching produces a homogeneous alloy structure with uniformly dispersed elements.
Faster cooling shortens the time available for atomic diffusion.
A slower quench permits sufficient atomic mobility for phase separation or elemental segregation.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will be single-phase HEAs.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles will have high surface-atom exposure.
Slower-cooled nanoparticles will exhibit phase-separated or segregated morphologies.
Slower-cooled nanoparticles will have diminished surface uniformity.
Phase separation, elemental segregation, or uncontrolled morphologies are typically observed under standard or slower quenching.
The proposed quenching mechanism applies primarily to rapid, high-temperature synthesis of noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles containing more than five elements.
The proposed quenching mechanism is not expected to apply under low-temperature or prolonged reaction conditions where bulk diffusion dominates.
The cooling-rate threshold for homogeneous alloy formation may depend on composition and processing scale.
Failure of increasing quench rate to improve homogeneity or suppress phase separation and segregation relative to the slower-cooling control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is explicitly applied after reduction, but the mechanism says faster cooling restricts diffusion 'during reduction.' Post-reduction cooling cannot directly alter diffusion that already occurred during the reduction step unless cooling overlaps with reduction, which is not specified.
